title: Ext4 I/O-manager write-path migration
summary: Move ext4 from the direct page-pager compatibility path to a write-capable neutral planner while preserving page-cache ownership and durable journal ordering.

write_sets.notes: This proposed master plan owns only its specification and record. Each implementation slice claims its code write set after prior plans release it.

steps.title: Add neutral I/O data-source leases and dependency graph
steps.notes: Completed with leased IoDataSource values, validated BackendBioGraph, default planner resume rejection, and BlockGraph transport. Existing variants remain compatibility adapters; L4 rejects graph execution with ENOSYS until a dependency scheduler exists.

steps.title: Make PageSlot writeback generation-safe under concurrent redirty
steps.notes: Landed redirty preservation, fsync-frontier classification, the missing Phase-0 PageContainer L4 compatibility baseline, and PageSlot dirty transitions for both planner and FsPageBacking write materialization. PageContainer now admits dirty pages to L4 writeback, retains PageCache leases through planning/execution, routes terminal WritebackFinished completion into the generation-checked slot FSM, and rolls back leases/marks/slots on unplanned or queue-rejected submission. FileFsyncSession captures the page-generation frontier once, submits only the captured generations, waits without duplicate admission, resubmits a captured redirty after its earlier writeback, and surfaces terminal backend errors. Compatibility FsPageBacking::flush_page remains until 6G hot-path cutover; this slice makes no durable fsync claim before 6E ordered JBD2 fencing.

steps.title: Implement ext4 read planner parity
steps.notes: Map extents and holes through BackendPlanner while retaining FsPageBacking fallback. BackendPageRequest now carries an L4-owned IoDataTarget for page-cache read DMA, MountPayload transports source plus target into BackendPlanner, and PageContainer leases a CachedFrame target across planning until matching completion installs the same pin into the page index. Ext4BlockGeometry and plan_read_request emit complete hole plans, mapped-extent L6 bios, or metadata-first continuations; BlockDeviceImage exposes geometry only when the caller supplies its registered DeviceKey. Ext4ReadPlanner separates mapping lookup from plan construction and never performs I/O in the mapping callback. Ext4FsInstance/MountedExt4 carry an optional BackendPlanner capability, public mount helpers accept planner injection, and Ext4MappingTable supplies a lock-protected metadata-first cache that can be filled after L6 completion. Production pager-to-table completion wiring remains next.

steps.title: Plan buffered ext4 writeback from PC frame sources
steps.notes: This is not a durable fsync claim until the ordered journal slice is complete.

steps.title: Add ordered JBD2 transaction graph, replay, and fsync fence
steps.notes: Data precedes journal commit; commit record is durable before fsync completes; checkpoint remains asynchronous.

steps.title: Add direct-I/O coherence then switch hot paths incrementally
steps.notes: O_DIRECT bypasses the PC cache but not range coherency, ext4 planning, or L6 scheduling.

risks: Treating a completed data bio as durable fsync before ordered JBD2 exists would violate the power-loss contract.
A writeback completion that clears a page redirtied after submission loses data.
A plan that holds PC, inode, journal, or range locks across I/O will preserve the current serialization bottleneck.
Direct I/O without reservation and invalidation creates stale PC data.
blockers: Active I/O-manager and ext4 design files are already modified in the current worktree; reconcile this plan into those files in their owning change rather than overwriting them.
